title: BEEF Partner Check
description: Partners watch each other shoot and check one cue at a time — Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow-through — giving specific feedback after each shot.

content.objective: Understand the four shooting checkpoints and recognise them in a partner's shot.
content.setup: Pairs share a basket; shooter three metres from the rim, partner beside them with the second ball.
content.organization: Five shots per cue, then swap roles.
instructions: Round 1 (Balance): the partner checks the feet are shoulder-width and the shooter lands in place.
Round 2 (Eyes): the partner checks the eyes stay on the target until the ball lands.
Round 3 (Elbow): the partner checks the elbow sits under the ball.
Round 4 (Follow-through): the partner checks the arm finishes high with the wrist relaxed.
After each shot the partner gives one sentence of feedback.
coachingPoints: Watch only the cue for that round.
Feedback is specific: 'Elbow was out' not 'bad shot'.
Shooter repeats a shot after a correction.
commonMistakes: Partners watching the ball instead of the shooter.
Trying to fix all four cues at once.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Partner gives feedback on two cues at once.
variations: Film shots on a phone and check together.
successCriteria: Partner identifies the cue correctly in most shots.
Shooter improves the corrected cue on the next shot.
content.gameApplication: Players who can self-correct their form keep their shot reliable without a coach watching.
